Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:10:1.english: With their wings - That they touched a vessel with their wings.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:10:2.english: The wind [generated] by their wings - This is [a case of] pebbles, for it is [caused by] its force.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:10:4.english: And they pecked - With their beak, which is called bec [in Old French].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:10:5.english: They raised dust - From the ground onto the dough.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:12:1.hebrew: חצי נזק נמי לא - דלא אשכחן חצי נזק אלא במשונה, אבל במידי דאורחיה לא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:12:1.english: [He should] not [pay] even half-damage - For we do not find half-damage except for an unusual [act], but for something that is its normal way, [we do] not.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:14:1.english: Which in [the case of] a zav is impure - [This] implies actual contact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:14:2.hebrew: שבזב טהור - כגון שזרק חפץ על אדם, הוי טהור; ובנזקין, כעין צרורות, חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:14:2.english: Which, in [the case of] a zav, is ritually pure - For example, if he threw an object at a person, [the person] is ritually pure; and in [the case of] damages, [it is] like pebbles [tzerorot], [for which one pays] half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:15:1.english: Did he come to teach us [the law of] pebbles - [This is] a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:15:2.hebrew: עגלה מושכת בקרון - אתא לאשמועינן דבזב טמא, אם הלכה קרון שהזב עליה על גבי כלים, טמאים משום מדרס הזב; ובנזקין נמי, עגלה שמשכה בקרון ע"ג כלים, כגופה הוי ולא כצרורות. ואם התיז צרורות מתחת הקרון, דבזב טהור, בנזקין נמי צרורות נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:15:2.english: A calf pulling a cart - [Rava] comes to teach us that in [the case of] a zav it is ritually impure: if a cart upon which the zav is [riding] goes over vessels, they become ritually impure due to midras [treading-impurity] of the zav; and in [the case of] damages as well, a calf that pulled a cart over vessels is [considered] like [damage by] its own body and not like pebbles. And if it kicked up pebbles from underneath the cart, which in [the case of] a zav is ritually pure, in [the case of] damages as well, they are [considered] pebbles.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:18:1.english: After the initial [action] - When it pushed it, and with its body [it] broke the vessel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:19:1.english: And broke it with a stick - Before it came to rest.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:19:2.hebrew: פטור - המשברו, וחייב הזורק. אלמא בתר מעיקרא אזלינן, והואיל וסופו לישבר לכשינוח, כמי ששברו הוא דמי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:19:2.english: Exempt - [i.e.,] the one who breaks it [is exempt], and the thrower is liable. Thus, we follow the initial [cause], and since it is destined to break when it comes to rest, it is considered as though he [already] broke it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:1:1.hebrew: היינו רגל היינו בהמה - מאי רגל ומאי בהמה דתני תרתי במתני'? הא חדא היא, ואמאי הדר תני הבהמה מועדת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:1:1.english: Foot is the same as animal - What is "foot" and what is "animal," that [the Tanna] teaches two [categories] in the Mishnah? Surely it is one [and the same], so why does he further teach "the animal is forewarned"?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:1:2.hebrew: תנא אבות - רגל ממש, שדרסה ברגליה. וסיפא קתני תולדות: הבהמה מועדת להלך כדרכה ולשבר בגופה ובשערה ובשליף שעליה דרך הלוכה, דתולדות דרגל הן, דהזיקה מצוי ואין כוונתה להזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:1:2.english: [The tanna] taught primary categories - [Referring to] actual [damage by] Foot, where [the animal] trampled with its feet. And the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches subcategories: “The animal is forewarned to walk in its normal manner and to break [objects] with its body, and with its hair, and with the saddlebag that is upon it in the course of its walking,” for they are subcategories of Foot, since its damage is common and its intention is not to cause damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:21:1.hebrew: הידוס ס"ד - אמאי לא ליהוו מועד? הא אורחיה הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:21:1.english: Hopping — does it enter your mind - Why would they not be forewarned? Indeed, it is its [normal] way.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:21:2.hebrew: הידוס והתיז - שגלגל הכלי ברקידתו למקום אחר ונשבר. מ"ד מועד לנזק שלם, סבר בתר מעיקרו אזלינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:21:2.english: Hopping and propelled - That [the chicken] rolled the vessel with its hopping to another place, and it broke. The one who says [that it is] forewarned [to pay] full damages holds [that] we follow its initial [action].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:2:1.hebrew: מאי אבות ומאי תולדות איכא - (והא) ליכא למימר דהאי דתנא בהמה מועדת לאכול פירות וירקות הוי להו תולדה, דהיינו שן ממש, ותולדה דשן היינו נתחככה בכותל להנאתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:2:1.english: What primary categories and what subcategories are there - (And) one cannot say that what it taught — "the animal is forewarned to eat fruits and vegetables" — is a subcategory, for that is Tooth proper, whereas a subcategory of Tooth is [when] it rubbed itself against a wall for its pleasure.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:2:2.english: He was responding to him - Rava [was responding] to Ravina.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:2:4.hebrew: וא"ל אנא שנאי חדא - רישא, ואת שני סיפא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:2:4.english: And he said to him: I resolved one - [namely,] the first clause, and you resolve the latter clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:1.english: And what is the reason - [It] refers to the latter clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:2.english: Be'irah [his animal] - That is the Aramaic translation of behemah [domesticated animal].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - מתני' דאשן דחיה נמי מיחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:3.english: It teaches us - The Mishnah [teaches us] that for Eating by an undomesticated animal, one is also liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:4.hebrew: דחיה בכלל בהמה - דכתיב (דברים י״ד:ד׳) ״זאת הבהמה אשר תאכלו״, ומפרש בתריה: איל, צבי ויחמור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:3:4.english: That an undomesticated animal is included in the category of domesticated animals - As it is written (Deuteronomy 14:4): "This is the animal [behemah] that you may eat," and afterwards it specifies: "hart, gazelle, and roebuck" [all of which are undomesticated animals].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:4:1.hebrew: אי הכי הא - שן בהמה מבעי ליה למיתני ברישא, והדר שן חיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:4:1.english: If so, this - [The case of] the tooth of a domesticated animal he should have taught first, and afterward [that of] the tooth of an undomesticated animal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:5:1.hebrew: רישא נמי ליתני - בהמה, דהוי תולדה, ברישא, דלא כתיבא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:5:1.english: [In] the first clause too, let [him] teach - [the case of] a domesticated animal, which is a subcategory, first, since it is not [explicitly] written.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:5:2.english: Both this and that - [The] tooth of a wild animal and [the] tooth of a domesticated animal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:5:4.english: He leaves aside a primary category and teaches a subcategory - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:6:1.hebrew: דסליק מרגל - בפ"ק (דף טו:) תנן הרגל מועדת, ולא תנן הבהמה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:6:1.english: [Since] he concluded with the foot - In the first chapter (15b), we learned [in the Mishnah], "The foot is forewarned," and we did not learn, "the animal."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:7:2.english: Shalif - A load that is in a sack or in leather bags.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:7:3.hebrew: סומכוס - לית ליה הלכתא דחצי נזק צרורות, אלא נזק שלם ס"ל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:7:3.english: Sumakhos - He does not accept the halakhah of half-damages [for] pebbles; rather, he holds [that one pays] full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:7:4.hebrew: נובר - בחוטמו, ובלע"ז פורי"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:7:4.english: Burrowing - With its snout; and in Old French, forer [to dig/bore].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:8:1.english: [It] propelled - For it was [a case of] pebbles.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:9:1.hebrew: צרורות כי אורחייהו - כלומר, אע"ג דאורחייהו להתיז צרורות, משלם חצי נזק, כדמפרש לקמיה דהלכתא גמירי לה. וכן חזיר הנובר ומתיז צרורות בחוטמו הוי נמי כצרורות דרגל, דכל מה שהוא כחו ולא גופו קרי צרורות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 17b:9:1.english: Pebbles in their typical manner - That is to say, even though it is their typical manner to propel pebbles, [the owner] pays half-damages, as [the Gemara] explains further on, that it is a law received by tradition. And similarly, a pig that burrows and propels pebbles with its snout is also like pebbles [propelled] by the foot, for anything that is [caused by] its force and not its body is called "pebbles."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:14:1.hebrew: כל שבזב טהור - אין זה הכלל דוקא, דהא קנה בקומטו של זב והסיט בו הטהור — טהור, ולענין נזקין אין חילוק. וכל עיקר האי כללא לא בא אלא למעט זורק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:14:1.english: "Any [case] where in [the laws of] a zav [it is] pure" - This general rule is not exact, for [in the case of] a reed in the fold [of the body] of a zav with which he moved a pure [person], [the pure person] is pure, yet with regard to damages there is no distinction. Rather, the entire purpose of this rule was only to exclude [the case of] throwing.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:18:1.hebrew: בתר מעיקרא אזלינן כו' - ומדתנן "דרסה על הכלי ושברתו", דמשמע הא נתגלגל למקום אחר ונשבר שם חייב ח"נ — ליכא למידק; דאדרבה, מדמפליג בין ראשון לשני ולא מפליג בראשון גופיה, איכא למידק איפכא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:18:1.english: Do we follow the initial [action], etc. - And from that which we learned [in the Mishnah], "If it trod upon a vessel and broke it," which [might seem to] imply that if it rolled to another place and broke there, [the owner] is liable for half damages — one cannot infer [this]; for on the contrary, from the fact that [the Mishnah] distinguishes between the first [vessel] and the second [vessel] and does not distinguish within the first [vessel] itself, one can infer the opposite.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:19:1.hebrew: זרק כלי מראש הגג כו' - נראה דאם זרק אבן או חץ על הכלי, ובא אחר וקדם ושברו — דפשיטא דחייב, ולא שייך כאן "מנא תבירא תבר"; דאי אזלינן נמי הכא בתר מעיקרא, לא משכחת בצרורות ח"נ. וסברא פשוטה היא לחלק בין זורק אבן לזורק כלי עצמו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:19:1.english: "[If] one threw a vessel from the top of the roof, etc." - It appears that if [one] threw a stone or an arrow at a vessel, and another [person] came and preceded [it] and broke [the vessel], it is obvious that [the second person] is liable, and [the principle of] "he broke a broken vessel" does not apply here; for if we were to follow the initial [act] here as well, you would not find half-damages in [the case of] pebbles [tzerorot]. And it is a straightforward reasoning to distinguish between one who throws a stone and one who throws the vessel itself.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:3:1.hebrew: סד"א ושלח את בעירה כתיב - אע"ג דכבר אשמועינן ברישא דאפי' תרנגולין מועדין, מ"מ ניחא ליה לאשמועינן גבי שן. וקשה קצת: אמאי לא תנא נמי תולדה בשן כמו ברגל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:3:1.english: It enters your mind to say that it is written: “And he set his animal loose” - Even though [the Mishnah] already taught us in the first clause that even chickens are forewarned, nevertheless it prefers to teach us [this] regarding Eating. And it is somewhat difficult: why did it not also teach a derivative for Eating, just as [it did] for Trampling?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:3:2.hebrew: קמ"ל דחיה בכלל בהמה - לא מההיא דרשה דבהמה המקשה (חולין דף עא.) קאמר הכא דחיה בכלל בהמה, דהא הכא אפילו עוף נמי הוי בכלל בהמה, כדקתני: "התרנגולת מועדת"; אלא ילפינן "בהמה" משבת, כדאמרינן בס"פ הפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף נד:), ד"בעירה" ו"בהמה" הכל אחד, דמתרגמינן בהמה — בעירה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:3:2.english: [The Gemara] teaches us that an undomesticated animal is included in [the category of] domesticated animal - It is not from that exposition of [the chapter] Behemah HaMaksheh (Chullin 71a) that [the Gemara] says here that an undomesticated animal is included in [the category of] domesticated animal, for here even a bird is also included in [the category of] domesticated animal, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "The hen is forewarned"; rather, we derive [the meaning of] "domesticated animal" [behemah] from Shabbat, as we say at the end of the chapter HaParah (below, Bava Kamma 54b), that be'irah and behemah are all one [and the same], since we translate behemah [into Aramaic as] be'irah.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:7:1.hebrew: וחמור במשאו - אע"ג דכבר שנה בשליף שעליה, אצטריך לאשמועינן לפי שאין משאוי של חמור מהודק ומחובר בו כבשאר בהמה, וס"ד דלא הוי כגופו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:7:1.english: Or a donkey with its burden - Even though [the baraita] already taught "with the saddlebag that is on it," it was necessary to teach us [this case], because a donkey's burden is not tightly fastened and attached to it as with other animals, and one might have thought that it is not [considered] like its body.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:7:2.hebrew: נובר באשפה - "יכרסמנה חזיר מיער" (תהילים פ׳:י״ד) מתרגמינן: ינובריניה. ואע"ג דתנא צרורות דרגל, אשמועינן צרורות דשן, דלהנאתו קעביד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 17b:7:2.english: Burrowing [nover] in the garbage heap - [The verse] "The boar from the forest ravages it [yekharsemennah]" (Psalms 80:14) we translate [in the Targum as] yenovrinneih. And even though [the Tanna already] taught pebbles of Regel [foot damage], he teaches us [here] pebbles of Shen [tooth damage], since [the pig] does [this] for its own benefit.
